To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) our online action recognition system can be combined with most existing frame-by-frame feature descriptions and achieves state-of-the-art performance on standard benchmarks; (ii) the performance of our system is comparable to that of the state-of-the-art, non-incremental, nonparametric baselines and it is superior to the state-of-the- art, incremental, parametric baselines.
We introduce an online system for action recognition that can be combined, in real time, with any set of feature descriptors.

we introduce an online action classification system that can be used in real time, that does not require to trim videos to the same length, that can be trained incrementally, that does not need any parameter tuning and that can be used for continuous action recognition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing methods for learning and predicting the temporal evolution of a multivariate time series.
the following questions.
incremental learning and classification of multivariate time series, which are a natural representation of video data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper is a well written, clearly presented and interesting paper that provides a novel approach to action recognition.

the proposed system is able to achieve state-of-the-art performance for action recognition, with the following advantages: (i) incremental training, (ii) frame by frame prediction, (iii) nonparametric predictive model, (iv) no need to trim the videos to equal length, (v) video segmentation for continuous recognition, (vi) no need for a separate tuning phase.
the system proposed in this thesis is an efficient and effective online action recognition system, which can be combined with a variety of frame-by-frame features.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we introduce a novel incremental online action recognition system which is able to learn the action classes from the data and adapt its model to the complexity of the task.
we introduce an online action classification system that covers the frame feature spaces with a non-parametric predictive model.
we have developed the first incremental action recognition algorithm that can be used as a plug-in for any action recognition system that uses frame by frame feature vectors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the problem of action recognition is not about finding better features, but about finding a way to combine them in a nonparametric way.
we can use the same classifier for both action recognition and video segmentation.
we have introduced a novel nonparametric incremental learning framework for multivariate time series.
